mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over time signals an easing monetary policy cycle, which reduces discount rates applied to equity cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns in easing periods are not statistically significantly higher than a baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the INDPRO index over time reflects growing production capacity and demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations rise.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth does not correlate with SPX 60d returns (R² < 0.05) or SPX returns are negative despite rising INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in UNRATE above 4.5% in the next month signals weakening labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investor sentiment turns cautious.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4.5% in the next month
failure_condition: UNRATE crosses above 4.5% but SPX 5d returns remain positive, or the effect persists beyond the 5-day window without reversal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in FEDFUNDS above 5.0% in the next month signals aggressive monetary tightening, compressing equity valuations and generating negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.0% in the next month
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.0% but SPX 20d returns stay positive, or the effect is not significant (p > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in quarterly demand (GDPC1) and monthly supply (INDPRO) signal robust economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and INDPRO both increase in the same month
failure_condition: GDPC1 and INDPRO increases do not precede SPX 20d returns (lagged) or the correlation is weak (R² < 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in FEDFUNDS rates and rise in UNRATE signals contractionary monetary policy and labor market weakening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investor confidence declines.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases while UNRATE increases in the same month
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS down and UNRATE up but SPX 5d returns remain positive, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, rising FEDFUNDS rates signal contractionary policy, which compresses equity valuations and generates negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as risk aversion increases.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns remain positive during tightening cycles, or the effect is not significant (p > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: In a labor market recovery regime (UNRATE below 4.5%), falling UNRATE rates signal strengthening labor demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate investment accelerates.
failure_condition: UNRATE falls below 4.5% but SPX 60d returns do not rise significantly (p > 0.05) or the effect is inconsistent across regimes.
